findings.message: The Owner-line parser only matches a bare email, optionally in backticks, placed right after `**Owner:**`. Both READMEs give the format as `**Owner:** <email>`. Written that way, with angle brackets, the line doesn't parse, because `<` and `>` are in the excluded character class. The usual `Name <email>` form fails too, because the name comes first. In both cases `owner` silently becomes null and `ownerEmailOf` falls back to whoever committed `change.md`, so the person the repo names is ignored. Fix: find the email anywhere on the Owner line (for example `/\*\*Owner:\*\*[^\n]*?<?`?([^\s`<>·]+@[^\s`<>·]+)`?>?/`). Then regenerate `plugins/amax/scripts/read-specclaw.mjs` and add the bracketed and `Name <email>` forms to the AC-7 reader test.
findings.scenario: Header `**Owner:** <kasun@lumenlabs.test>` or `**Owner:** Kasun Dias <kasun@lumenlabs.test>`, with change.md committed by maya@lumenlabs.test → `readSpecclaw` gives `owner: null` → the proposal is owned by Maya, not Kasun.

findings.message: The rule for when a sync must leave the stored owner alone (`owner_set_by_person`, or the email is unknown) is written twice. One copy is the SQL `personSet` in `upsertSpecProposal`. The other is the early return in `repoOwnerStale` (`server/owner.ts`). The two agree today. If either is edited alone, the 'unchanged' short-circuit and the actual write can disagree, giving a needless rewrite or a missed one. Fix: derive both from one predicate, or have the upsert take the frozen flag from `repoOwnerStale`'s own check.

`SyncInput` now has `ownerEmail`, but the `sync_proposal` tool passes only a fixed list of fields to `syncProposal` and leaves `ownerEmail` out. A caller's `ownerEmail` is accepted and then silently dropped, so it reads as "couldn't be read": a new row gets no owner and an existing row keeps its owner. Either pass it through or remove it from the tool's input schema, so callers can't think it was applied.
findings.scenario: sync_proposal { key: FLT-210, ..., ownerEmail: 'nimal@lumenlabs.test' } on a new key → stored owner_user_id null, with no error

findings.message: `sameOnMain` treats a squash- or rebase-merged branch as merged only while its change folder on `main` is byte-identical to the branch's copy. If `main` edits that folder after the merge, before it's archived (status.md, a verify note), the branch counts as open again. CI then pushes it on every run, amax skips it as stale and sets needsReview, and the Repo sync card shows "Needs you" until the change is archived or the branch is deleted. A better rule: the branch's tip commit time is older than `main`'s last commit that touched the folder, or the branch tree is an ancestor state of `main`'s folder.
findings.scenario: squash-merge specclaw/105-x, then commit an edit to .specclaw/changes/105-x/status.md on main → the next CI run pushes specclaw/105-x → 'FLT-105: stale …' and needsReview true

findings.message: The AC-2 branch guard compares against any stored `source_ref`, including a proposal that was withdrawn because its folder was deleted from `main`. A new branch that reuses that number is then refused as "two changes numbered NNN", but no second folder exists anywhere. The CI's `taken` check doesn't see this case. Leave out withdrawn rows (`meta.withdrawn`), or give the skip its own wording so the reason isn't false.
findings.scenario: main deletes 302-other (FLT-302 is withdrawn); push ref specclaw/302-new → skipped 'two changes numbered 302: 302-other, 302-new', needsReview on every push

findings.message: The backfill reads `core.audit_event` from inside a delivery migration. The module standard says migrations touch only the module's own schema. It also depends on the audit row format: any owner set that was audited under another action or resource stays false, and the next sync overwrites it. Write down why this cross-schema read is allowed, or do the backfill in a one-off script owned by the platform.
